title: Tenant-priority signal orchestrator for usage/cost/latency alerts
creator: Anika Patel
description: Problem: The current alerting pipeline generates too many noisy notifications for usage/cost/latency spikes across tenants. Root causes include naive global thresholds, seasonal/rollup effects, and no tenant-level prioritization. Goal: Build a signal orchestrator that scores and prioritizes tenant-level telemetry signals, applies probabilistic suppression for low-value noise, and routes high-priority signals into the human-facing pager/alerting tiers. The orchestrator should integrate with existing anomaly scoring outputs, be region-aware, support tenant SLAs, and expose per-tenant rationale in the console.
acceptance_criteria: Signal scoring service ingests per-tenant metric streams and outputs a ranked list of events with priority tags (critical/high/medium/low)
False positive rate reduced by >=40% on historical replay of March 2026 bursts without increasing mean time to detect P1 incidents
Alert routing honors tenant SLA and configured notification channel (email/pager/slack) and can be toggled per-tenant
Dashboard shows per-tenant prioritized queue, suppression counts, and top contributing features for each scored event
Runbook updated with playbook for escalations and observed mitigations
implementation_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Console, Telemetry, and SRE. Agreed on scoring features and minimum integration points.

2026-03-05: Prototype of tenant-priority model (logistic regressor) that uses recent z-score, rate-of-change, tenant spend, and SLA weight — initial results show 30% fewer low-value alerts on a 7-day window.

2026-03-09: Built event contract for orchestrator -> router (fields: tenant_id, metric, ts, score, priority, rationale_tags). Draft PR opened for schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/487
2026-03-12: A/B test plan approved; will run orchestrator in parallel for 72h against production read-only pipeline and compare noise/recall metrics.
2026-03-14: Addressed reviewer feedback to include region and model-variant context in rationale_tags. Working on integration tests for suppression logic.
comments: PM review (Lena Cho): Please ensure the priority score is explainable in the console; product needs top-3 contributing reasons for each alert.
Design feedback (Priyanka Singh): Add an affordance to override suppression per-tenant from the tenant settings page.
SRE note (Oliver Kline): Ensure the orchestrator operates in a fail-open mode; if it fails, alerts should degrade to existing pipeline without loss.
Eng review (Marco Ruiz): Will add sampling hooks to keep cost under budget during initial rollout.
tech_decisions: Scoring model: start with lightweight logistic regression with feature store-backed inputs; move to XGBoost if needed for recall after A/B results
Suppression strategy: probabilistic suppression with configurable tenant override and cooldown windows (default 15min)
Data retention: keep raw scored events for 30 days and summarized aggregate for 90 days to support replay and tuning
Failure mode: fail-open to existing alerts; orchestrator runs as a sidecar of the router service for locality
testing_plan: Replay historical telemetry from Jan-Mar 2026 and compare alert volume/precision against baseline
A/B run in production read-only for 72 hours with metrics collection (precision, recall, time-to-detect, suppressed_count)
Integration tests: contract tests for orchestrator->router event schema and end-to-end smoke test that exercises suppression toggles
Load test: ensure orchestrator handles peak ingestion (100k tenant events/min) with <200ms p95 scoring latency
